merged.title: fix(hostgen): fail the assembly guard only on translations code reaches
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Since #532, a rac1 build made with the disc stops in hostgen: rac1 PAL fails with 260 errors of the form `func_… runs as its assembly (translated from it), and the program reach it`.

#532's assembly guard fails every function hostgen translates from the disc's assembly, whether or not anything reaches it. A build without the disc translates nothing, so CI never runs into this. Builds with the disc do: rac1's programs translate many functions that no translated code calls (260 in PAL alone), and adding them to `assembly_allow` is no way out, because a disc-less build would then fail them as unused rows.

- `assembly_guard` keeps every translation in the report's `assembly_reached`, but fails only one that a translated caller reaches, the same as a stub without the disc.
- `AssemblyGuard` tests: an unreached translation is listed but passes; a reached one fails.

rac2 is unaffected. Its allowed rows all have callers, and its translated routines have their own C since #532.

merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:

merged.title: fix: skip textures made anew each tick in the texture dump
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
The texture dump wrote thousands of junk files into `Interface/`. rac1 uploads a 64x64 texture on every tick on each planet. It is fully transparent and a few texels change by 1 each tick, so every tick gave a new hash and a new file. No pack can replace these.

## After
Only real textures are dumped. On rac1 NTSC-U levels 0-5, `Interface/` went from 2399 files to 86. All removed files were those transparent 64x64 textures. `Planets/`, `Shared/` and `Animated/` stay the same.

## How
- `texture_pack::LiveWatch` watches each upload place. A place that gets a new, never seen texture on 64 ticks in a row (at most 4 ticks apart) is live: it is not dumped, and the files this run already wrote for it are removed.
- Animation cycles are not affected: their frames come back, so they never reach 64 new ones. Many new textures in one tick count once.
- A held texture that is still drawn more than 4 ticks later (a fade's last picture) is dumped once.
- Only the dump changes. Game logic

merged.title: fix(tools): us_port.py renames the names of a port in one pass
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
us_port.py turned each relocated name into its NTSC-U address one name at a time. When the
NTSC-U address of one name is the PAL address of another name the block also uses, the second
rename caught the first one's result as well, and the two names became one: a port that reads two
globals would read one of them twice. The same could happen to the function's own name and to the
callee twins renamed after it.

The renames are now made in one pass (rename_all), so a new name is never renamed again. Where no
new name is another name's old one, the output is the same as before. Codex's NTSC-U porting
adapter hit this in level 33 (two level globals merged in func_L33_0034DE80; its relocation audit
caught it), which is how the pattern was found; this is the same loop in the repository's tool.
tests/test_us_port.py covers the chained case, whole-word matching and the name forms.

`tools/sister_twins.py` finds rac3 functions that are still in assembly and whose code is a function another OpenRAC decompilation has already matched in C. merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## What

`tools/check_return_types.py`, a **report-only** check. It is adapted from rac2-decomp's `tests/check_return_types.py` (005bfc4dd).

- It parses every `.c` under `src/` with clang (`-fsyntax-only -Xclang -ast-dump=json`, MIPS target, `-I include -I .`).
- It reduces every definition and declaration to the class the EE ABI returns it in: void, int32, int64, int128, float, double (soft-float, `$v0`), pointer, aggregate. Declarations include file scope, block scope, headers, and C89 implicit declarations at a call.
- It groups them by the function the build links them to, and lists each group whose classes differ, for PAL and NTSC-U separately.

Each file still matches retail on its own. But a port that links all the C together reads the result from the wrong register when the classes disagree. In rac2, a float definition read as int silenced every 3D sound.

opened.title: fix(tools): us_port.py renames the names of a port in one pass
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
us_port.py turned each relocated name into its NTSC-U address one name at a time. When the
NTSC-U address of one name is the PAL address of another name the block also uses, the second
rename caught the first one's result as well, and the two names became one: a port that reads two
globals would read one of them twice. The same could happen to the function's own name and to the
callee twins renamed after it.

The renames are now made in one pass (rename_all), so a new name is never renamed again. Where no
new name is another name's old one, the output is the same as before. Codex's NTSC-U porting
adapter hit this in level 33 (two level globals merged in func_L33_0034DE80; its relocation audit
caught it), which is how the pattern was found; this is the same loop in the repository's tool.
tests/test_us_port.py covers the chained case, whole-word matching and the name forms.

## Purpose

`tools/sister_twins.py` finds rac3 functions that are still in assembly and whose code is a function another OpenRAC decompilation has already matched in C. The sister's C can then be ported instead of written again. A twin is **exact** when every relocation-masked word is equal, and **near** (20 words and more) when at least 95 % of them are.

The tool turns the one-off scan scripts of 2026-11-15 into a reusable tool. That scan found 203 twins (179 exact), and porting their C gave dozens of matches.

opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

`tools/check_return_types.py`, a **report-only** check. It is adapted from rac2-decomp's `tests/check_return_types.py` (005bfc4dd).

- It parses every `.c` under `src/` with clang (`-fsyntax-only -Xclang -ast-dump=json`, MIPS target, `-I include -I .`).
- It reduces every definition and declaration to the class the EE ABI returns it in: void, int32, int64, int128, float, double (soft-float, `$v0`), pointer, aggregate. Declarations include file scope, block scope, headers, and C89 implicit declarations at a call.
- It groups them by the function the build links them to, and lists each group whose classes differ, for PAL and NTSC-U separately.

Each file still matches retail on its own. But a port that links all the C together reads the result from the wrong register when the classes disagree. In rac2, a float definition read as int silenced every 3D sound.
